And don't forget to try the yummy bubble tea, like the strawberry flavor!

input: I recently tried out this Thai restaurant and I would give it 4-5 stars. It was my first visit and I found the food to be delicious. The shrimp spring rolls were especially fresh and the peanut sauce was tasty. The tom yum soup was a bit too spicy for my liking, but still had a good sour flavor. The pad thai and drunken noodle dishes were also enjoyable, although the noodles in the pad thai were a bit overdone. The portions were slightly smaller than other places in the area. The owner was friendly and attentive, even coming outside to talk with me about the food. The restaurant has a cute setup in a quaint house, but it may not be ideal if it's crowded. Overall, I think it's worth a try for Thai food fans. I used a Living Social deal, which made the total bill for two people, including an appetizer, soup, and a drink, to be around $24.

input: My husband and I reserved a Corolla-sized car online, but requested an upgrade to a Camry at Avis Rent A Car in Reno. After some discussion, we received the Camry we wanted. The staff was professional, but the rental price of $800 for five days seemed high. We had already purchased insurance for $150. The car itself was great during our vacation. However, upon dropping off the car, we found out that a weekly rate would have been just $15 more. The upgrade had cost us an extra $20 per day. I will not rent from Avis again, opting for Hertz or Dollar and making phone reservations instead. In hindsight, the extra insurance was unnecessary as my personal insurance covers everything.

input: I had a great experience taking my boyfriend for a tour and beer sampling at Yuengling on a Saturday. We were pleasantly surprised by how close it was to us. Before going, make sure to check the website for tour times and read the FAQ's. We noticed some people wearing flip flops on the tour, even though closed toe shoes are insisted upon. It's worth noting that there is no production on Saturdays, so the brewery was quiet and empty. The tour itself was about 40 minutes long and started with a video about the history of Yuengling. Our guide was knowledgeable and took us through various parts of the brewery. The highlight was the tasting room, where we got to try different beers for free (tips encouraged). Unfortunately, they were out of a few beers that day. Overall, it was a great tour and I plan on revisiting with my parents.

input:
I heard about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite and decided to give it a try with my SO. We went on a Saturday morning and had to wait in line. 

The takoyaki appetizer was delicious - perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. The fried octopus was good but didn't come with enough mayo. 

Unfortunately, the ramen noodles were overcooked and didn't fit well with the dishes. The broth was flavorful, but the red chili one was too spicy and covered up the depth. I preferred the black garlic broth. 

Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced. The decor was nice, but there were screaming kids running around which made our meal unpleasant.

input: Overall, this restaurant is small but conveniently located on the wharf. Despite the limited seating, the wait time was short. Sitting at the bar was a good option. As a non-seafood enthusiast, I was pleasantly surprised by the shrimp and onion rings. However, my seafood enthusiast husband did not enjoy the crab sandwich. If you love shellfish and appreciate the great location, this place could be worth a try.

input: Finally tried this place after passing by so many times and I'm glad we did. Despite the small size, the interior is visually pleasing with wooden palates and two-tone gray walls. input: This is a typical Broad Ripple charming spot with a small, trendy, and bustling atmosphere. Unfortunately, they do not take reservations, which can be annoying for those traveling from another part of town. However, the cocktails were creative and delicious, and the server's suggestions were on point. The guacamole was tasty, but came with nuts despite requesting them to be left off. The Harvest salad was a highlight with its delightful combination of fruit and root vegetables. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both delicious, accompanied by interesting white sweet mashed potatoes. The Tostones were a bit dry, but dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great. Unfortunately, there were no gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options available. Overall, it's worth a visit, just make sure to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to secure a table.

Nevertheless, their inventive and delicious cocktails, coupled with the server's spot-on recommendations, make for a satisfying experience. On the other hand, their Harvest salad steals the spotlight with its delightful amalgamation of fruity and earthy flavors. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both scrumptious, accompanied by the intriguing touch of white sweet mashed potatoes. Unfortunately, those seeking gluten-free and dairy-free dessert options will be disappointed as none were available. Despite the minor setbacks, this place is definitely worth a visit. Just remember to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to ensure snagging a table.

input: I've been to Jackson's multiple times and finally decided to leave a review. The panini Reuben was delicious with great use of garlic and perfectly sliced meat. However, the salad came out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not ideal, and the presentation was a bit sloppy. The sandwich was served directly on a plate instead of a napkin, causing the bread to get soggy if it sits for too long. The price is a bit high, but the food and drink quality justifies it. They have a great selection of wines and beers to choose from. The wait staff is generally friendly but can sometimes be short or distracted. The wait time for drinks can vary, with my longest wait being 15 minutes during a lunch rush. Overall, it was a good experience and I will return.

input: My girlfriends and I dined at the Creole House for dinner due to its proximity to our hotel. The bacon garlic oysters were average, as the flavors were overpowered by the cheese and bacon. The jumbo buffalo wings were tasty and well-seasoned. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite, while the blackened red fish was just okay. The sautéed veggies accompanying the dish were excessively salty. The canal street red fish wasn't great and lacked garlic sauce. The paddle boat drinks tasted good but were more juice than alcohol. Overall, the food was underwhelming, earning the restaurant a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, provided excellent hospitality and tried his best to ensure our satisfaction.

However, we were pleasantly surprised by the jumbo buffalo wings, which were delicious and perfectly seasoned.

Additionally, the sautéed veggies served alongside the fish were excessively salty, greatly diminishing our enjoyment of the dish. The canal street red fish wasn't particularly great either, as it lacked the promised garlic sauce.

On the bright side, the paddle boat drinks were enjoyable, although we felt that they leaned more towards being fruity juices rather than alcoholic beverages. All in all, the food at the Creole House left us feeling underwhelmed, leading us to award the restaurant a solid 3-star rating.

On a positive note, we received exceptional service from our server, Alexander. He went above and beyond to ensure our satisfaction, providing us with excellent hospitality throughout our dining experience.

input: This is hands down my favorite sushi spot in Delaware. The menu is simple yet executed perfectly, with reasonably priced rolls that are bursting with fish.
